episodes.174835: An upper level trough moved into West Texas while a surface low developed along an old frontal boundary over the Gulf of Mexico. This low brought the old boundary back northward as a warm front, and thunderstorms developed in this warm air advection. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.175031: A surface low developed in southeast Texas early November 26th and tracked northeast towards central Arkansas throughout the day. At the same time, a cold front tracked across western Louisiana while a warm front lifted north across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi. Moisture rich unstable air within this warm sector over the local area provided the environment to support a few severe thunderstorms. Severe winds, a tornado and flash flooding occurred with this event.

A tornado touched down on Highway 90 and just south of Bayou|Gauche Road, peeling the roof off a house and a car port as well|as flipping a RV. Extensive tree damage was noted around the|property and to the northwest as well as debris thrown a|significant distance. North of Bayou Gauche Road, a church|complex had roof damage to most of the buildings as well as a|flipped RV. These buildings were noted to have also been damaged|from Ida, with blue tarps on the roofs still. One brand new roof,|though, did have notable damage to the southeast corner. As the|tornado moved northwest across Highway 90, mostly tree damage and|light structural damage, such as shingles and siding damage, were|noted before the tornado quickly lifted.

A tornado touched down near Hickory Field Rd in Talisheek in association with an embedded supercell thunderstorm. This tornado quickly intensified causing visible damage to numerous trees including numerous uprooted trees just east of Cow Hammock Lake. This debris was visible via tornado debris signature on KLIX radar imagery in association with this circulation. Maximum width of the tornado was estimated via this swath of damage on satellite imagery. The tornado quickly occluded north over inaccessible land west of the Bogue Chitto River. Survey and analysis of this tornado damage path was conducted via high resolution satellite imagery from November 18 and 27, 2022 and supplemented by higher resolution data that could depict extent of tree damage in March 2024.
